headline: Weight Surgery, measured at a fair horizon
lede: The shipped Weight Surgery demo answered 'could forge-Qwen do what Astra did?' with a no — but every measurement ran at a 1024-token cap where answers can't finish at all. Slot a re-ran Jon's full procedure at cap 4096: the base model finishes 9/12 there, the tight-loop class nearly vanishes (0/3 repeats), and an all-layer scan rediscovered MIT's layer 19 without the prior. Held-out scoring (fixed 100+100, base/edit/penalty rows) runs overnight; the demo page updates with provable numbers.

notes.text: #1506: fair-horizon rescore in flight — cap 4096 (base finishes 9/12), per-layer loop-direction scan over all 24 layers (L23 t=7.7, L19 t=5.9), edit k256 = 0.070% of weights
Practice verdict at the fair cap: the edit currently HURTS termination (4/12 → 2/12) — the L23 direction partially encodes the about-to-end signal; position-confound lesson logged on the issue

Evidence posted on #1493: the shipped verdict measured cap-truncation, not the fix (batches.jsonl shows every run at cap ≤1024, after the hold) — honest process, honest numbers, rescore filed and running
Overnight runner detached to launchd (nested launchctl refused in warden contexts) — resumable per-problem jsonl, merge tomorrow via PR #1510
